'''Maria (Masha) Gordina''' is a Russian-American mathematician.{{r|simons}} After serving as professor of mathematics at the [[University of Connecticut]] for many years, she is currently the John F. Randolph Professor in Mathematics at the University of Rochester and chair of the Department of Mathematics there.{{r|rochester}} Her research is at the interface between
[[stochastic analysis]], [[differential geometry]], and [[functional analysis]], including the study of [[heat kernel]]s on infinite-dimensional [[group (mathematics)|groups]].{{r|michler}}

Gordina is the daughter of  mathematician Mikhail (Misha) Gordin.<ref>[https://www2.math.uconn.edu/~gordina/Mikhail_Gordin/index.html Mikhail Gordin]</ref>

==Education and career==
Gordina earned a diploma in 1990 from [[Saint Petersburg State University|Leningrad State University]], and became an assistant professor at the [[Saint Petersburg Electrotechnical University|Leningrad Electrotechnical Institute]].{{r|cv}} She completed her doctorate in 1998 from [[Cornell University]]; her dissertation, ''Holomorphic functions and the heat kernel measure on an infinite dimensional complex orthogonal group'', was supervised by [[Leonard Gross]].{{r|cv|mgp}} Gordina held a post-doctoral appointment at [[McMaster University]]. She was awarded a National Science Foundation postdoctoral fellowship in 2000, and conducted research at  the [[University of California, San Diego]]. In 2003 Gordina joined the University of Connecticut faculty.{{r|cv}}

Gordina serves on the editorial boards of ''Forum Mathematicum'',<ref>[https://www.degruyter.com/view/journals/form/form-overview.xml?language=en/ Forum Mathematicum]</ref> the ''Electronic Journal of Probability'',<ref>[https://imstat.org/journals-and-publications/electronic-journal-of-probability/ Electronic Journal of Probability]</ref> and ''Electronic Communications in Probability''.<ref>[https://imstat.org/journals-and-publications/electronic-communications-in-probability/ Electronic Communications in Probability]</ref>

==Honors==
Gordina was awarded a Humboldt Research fellowship in 2005 (with renewals), and the [[Ruth I. Michler Memorial Prize]] of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in 2009. She was named a Simons Fellow <ref>[https://www.simonsfoundation.org/search/gordina Gordina, Simons Fellow]</ref> (2016) in Mathematics and Physical Sciences. She was named to the 2023 class of Fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]], "for contributions to stochastic and geometric analysis, infinite-dimensional analysis, and ergodicity of hypoelliptic diffusions".{{r|fams}}

==Selected publications==
* Baudoin, Fabrice; Feng, Qi; Gordina, Maria Integration by parts and quasi-invariance for the horizontal Wiener measure on foliated compact manifolds. J. Funct. Anal. 277 (2019), no. 5, 1362–1422.
* Banerjee, Sayan; Gordina, Maria; Mariano, Phanuel Coupling in the Heisenberg group and its applications to gradient estimates. Ann. Probab. 46 (2018), no. 6, 3275–3312.
* Eldredge, Nathaniel; Gordina, Maria; Saloff-Coste, Laurent Left-invariant geometries on SU(2) are uniformly doubling. Geom. Funct. Anal. 28 (2018), no. 5, 1321–1367.
* Baudoin, Fabrice; Gordina, Maria; [[Tai Melcher|Melcher, Tai]]. Quasi-invariance for heat kernel measures on sub-Riemannian infinite-dimensional Heisenberg groups. Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 365 (2013), no. 8, 4313–4350. 
* Driver, Bruce K.; Gordina, Maria Heat kernel analysis on infinite-dimensional Heisenberg groups. J. Funct. Anal. 255 (2008), no. 9, 2395–2461. 
* Cardetti, Fabiana; Gordina, Maria A note on local controllability on [[Lie group]]s. Systems Control Lett. 57 (2008), no. 12, 978–979. 
* Gordina, Maria Heat kernel analysis and Cameron-Martin subgroup for infinite dimensional groups. J. Funct. Anal. 171 (2000), no. 1, 192–232.
